commit.message:
core/integration: wait for the listener in TestHealthcheckCommand

TestServices/TestHealthcheckCommand/shell failed on main after the merge
of #14700 (artifact filter gaps), which doesn't touch services: the
client's curl got "Connection refused" from the service and exited 7 at
services_test.go:2463 (Cloud trace fe5d2ba01382924041b7dc8e9e25da69).

When a container has a Docker healthcheck, the engine runs it instead
of probing the exposed ports, and the first check runs as soon as the
container starts. The fixture's healthcheck only touched a marker file,
so the service could be declared ready before the app had bound :8080.

Make both forms of the healthcheck probe 127.0.0.1:8080 with busybox
nc -z first, and touch the marker only once that succeeds. The test
still checks that the healthcheck ran, through the marker the app
serves, and both the shell and the exec forms are kept. The exec form
now runs /bin/sh -c directly, to sequence the listener probe and the
marker creation while keeping the exec form's argument vector.

With a 3s sleep before ListenAndServe in the app, the old fixture fails
both subtests with curl exit 7, and this one passes both.

Signed-off-by: Erik Sipsma <erik@sipsma.dev>

engine: drop dead uses of internal/buildkit

Remove engine code that depended on internal/buildkit packages without
doing anything observable:

- daggerSession.containers was initialized and released on session
  removal, but nothing ever added an entry.
- progress.OneOff in imageexport wrote to the context's progress writer,
  which nothing installs.
- stack.Enable only attached a stack trace to exec exit errors, and
  stack.SetVersionInfo and apicaps.ExportedProduct only set values read
  by code the engine does not run.
- engineutil.StateIdx had no callers.

Replace appcontext.Context with a local signalContext that keeps the
same behavior: cancel on the first SIGTERM or SIGINT, print each signal,
exit on the third.

dagger-engine's cli app version now comes from engine.Version instead of
internal/buildkit/version, which was never set at link time.

Signed-off-by: Erik Sipsma <erik@sipsma.dev>

+// signalContext returns a context that is canceled on the first SIGTERM or
+// SIGINT. The third such signal forces the process to exit.
+func signalContext() context.Context {
+	const exitLimit = 3
+
+	signals := make(chan os.Signal, 2048)
+	signal.Notify(signals, unix.SIGTERM, unix.SIGINT)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancelCause(context.Background())
+	go func() {
+		for retries := 1; ; retries++ {
+			s := <-signals
+			fmt.Printf("Received signal %s, retries: %d/%d\n", s, retries, exitLimit)
+
+			err := fmt.Errorf("got %d SIGTERM/SIGINTs, forcing shutdown", retries)
+			cancel(err)
+			if retries >= exitLimit {
+				bklog.G(ctx).Error(err.Error())
+				os.Exit(1)
+			}
+		}
+	}()
+	return ctx
+}
+
